title: Ionic vs Covalent Bonds
guideExplore: Pick a bond type below, then watch how the electrons behave — transferred completely, or shared between atoms.
guideTransfer: Watch the electron travel all the way from Na to Cl. Once it fully transfers, charges appear: Na becomes Na⁺ and Cl becomes Cl⁻.
guideSharing: Watch the shared electron pair stay between the two nuclei, oscillating in place instead of moving to either atom.
learnMore: Ionic bonds form between a metal and a non-metal: one atom loses electrons, the other gains them, and the resulting ions attract each other. Covalent bonds form between non-metals that share electron pairs instead.
